first_delegated.default_label: Jul 3: Westminster (documented); Jul 2 night: place unresolved, marked

basis.text: Buford (27 Aug 1863, OR 27/1 p. 928; the second scan of the volume prints the date 'July 2'), Devin (6 Aug, p. 939) and Calef (27 Jul, p. 1032) put Gamble's and Devin's brigades at Taneytown on the night of 2 July and at Westminster on 3 July; Butterfield's order of 2 July (OR 27/3 p. 1086) and Pleasonton (31 Aug, p. 914) give Westminster, to guard the trains, as the destination. Merritt (18 Jul, p. 943) marched the Reserve Brigade to Emmitsburg on 2 July.

default.label: Taneytown on the night of 2 July, Westminster on 3 July (the Reserve Brigade: Emmitsburg)
default.note: Three questions: where the division spent the night of 2 July (Taneytown), where it was sent (Westminster, to guard the trains, reached on 3 July), and where its Reserve Brigade went (Emmitsburg, Merritt). Each source states one of these for its own unit and day.

witness.role: Colonel, 102d Pennsylvania Infantry (guarding a supply train)

support.note: Patterson (102d Pennsylvania, guarding a supply train; report of 4 Aug 1863): reached Westminster 'on the morning of the 2d' and reported there to 'General Buford'. He does not say which Buford; the division was at Gettysburg on the morning of 2 July.

inference.step: Patterson places a General Buford at Westminster on the morning of 2 July; read alone it would put Buford there a day early. The inference is only that Patterson's date or the officer is wrong or loose.

weighing.summary: The sources answer three questions. Where did Gamble's and Devin's brigades spend the night of 2 July? At Taneytown: Buford, Devin and Calef each say so for their own unit (Calef 'about 4 p. m.'). Where was the division sent? To Westminster, to guard the trains: Butterfield's order of 2 July and Pleasonton's report say so, and Buford, Devin and Calef say the brigades reached Westminster on 3 July. Where did Merritt's Reserve Brigade go on 2 July? To Emmitsburg, by Merritt's own report. The first pass left the night of 2 July unresolved because the date label in the first scan of Buford's report is garbled; the second scan reads 'July 2', and Devin and Calef need no scan. One source disagrees: Colonel Patterson (a train guard) says he reported to 'General Buford' at Westminster on the morning of 2 July; the division was at Gettysburg until the Third Corps relieved it, so that date is wrong or loose.
weighing.who: Buford commanded the division; Devin commanded the Second Brigade and Calef a battery of the First; Merritt commanded the Reserve Brigade; Pleasonton commanded the Cavalry Corps; Butterfield was Meade's chief of staff and wrote the order; Patterson commanded an infantry regiment guarding a train; Gamble's own report gives no place for 2 July.
weighing.when: Calef 27 Jul 1863, Merritt 18 Jul, Devin 6 Aug, Buford 27 Aug, Pleasonton 31 Aug, Patterson 4 Aug; Butterfield's order is of the day. All are within two months. The order of the day outranks the reports on what was ordered; each report outranks the others on its own unit.
weighing.where: Buford, Devin and Calef were with their units; Merritt at Emmitsburg; Pleasonton and Butterfield at corps and army headquarters; Patterson at Westminster.
weighing.how_knew: Each unit commander states where his own command went; Butterfield wrote the order; Pleasonton directed the movement; Patterson speaks of a meeting at Westminster.
weighing.clock: Calef's 'about 4 p. m.' at Taneytown is a Union clock reading; no other hour is used. The 20-minute clock difference is not applied and does not touch the point.
weighing.independence: Buford, Devin, Calef and Merritt are separate units and separate lines of knowledge; Pleasonton and Butterfield are orders; the Itinerary is a compilation from the reports, counted with them.

source_panel_text: On Jul 2 Buford's brigades (Gamble, Devin) went to Taneytown for the night (Buford, Devin, Calef) and on Jul 3 to Westminster to guard the trains (ordered Jul 2); Merritt's Reserve Brigade went to Emmitsburg. The three places answer different questions. One train guard has Buford at Westminster on the morning of Jul 2; four other values are listed.
